learning_design.input: Qualified current dated ordinary hospitality/cleaning dossiers identify sector/site/jurisdiction, necessary actual standards and legislation topics, primary references, workplace/client instructions, task conditions and responsible review. A new area/product or jurisdiction changes applicability; no universal permanent legal register is claimed.
learning_design.task: Explain every required current topic and its applicable source/role, check actual conditions and distinguish knowledge from observed compliant performance. Refresh missing/outdated sources and retain unresolved scope instead of calling a copied register complete.
outputs: Covers complete current source sector health/safety/hygiene/environment knowledge
Retains current register, jurisdiction, task and knowledge/performance boundaries

understanding_check.what_changes: The register has safety entries but omits a current required hygiene or environmental topic.
understanding_check.materials: Actual benign current required-topic list and explicitly incomplete source register.
expected_evidence: The required omitted actual topic remains missing.
Safety entries alone do not cover the complete source scope.
understanding_check.evidence_scope: Record the changed case, result and support used. A supplied-case result does not establish general or independent mastery.

difficulties.misconception: Counting a safety poster or one rule as complete sector-regulation knowledge.
difficulties.feedback: Reconcile every current required topic, applicable source and responsible review.

effort.spacing: Use separate revisits with changed examples and responsive breaks; no fixed age or calendar timetable is assumed.
effort.basis: Atlas author judgement for planning; no learner timing observations or instructional validation.
assumptions: Access, materials and the stated support are available.
Active time excludes setup, waiting, breaks and learning unrelated prerequisites.
The planning range is provisional; repeated occupational practice can take longer and is not inferred from successful card tasks.
Any retained earlier illustrative hour estimate describes the previous draft, not observed timing for this revised activity.
